title: Detecting health misinformation using machine learning and graph convolutional networks
author: Khemani, Patil, et al.

steps.title: Collect tweets via Streaming API
steps.instruction: Configure Twitter’s streaming API to retrieve real‑time tweets containing the keywords “COVID‑19”, “coronavirus”, “pandemic”, “health”, “healthcare”, “cancer”, “Ayurveda”, and other misinformation‑related hashtags; set language, geographic, and tweet‑type filters as needed; continuously collect tweets into a raw dataset.

steps.title: Annotate and label tweets
steps.instruction: From the collected stream, create a CSV with two columns (tweet text, label). Using the official Google web pages as reference, assign the label “reliable” to 8 958 tweets and “unreliable” to 6 677 tweets, yielding a total of 15 635 labeled tweets.

steps.title: Preprocess raw dataset
steps.instruction: Clean the CSV by removing empty columns, URLs, punctuation, and any HTML tags; then apply the following text‑processing steps in order:

substeps.instruction: Convert all text to lowercase (or uppercase) for consistency.
Strip noisy characters (special symbols, extra whitespace).
Tokenize the cleaned sentences into individual words or sub‑words.

steps.title: Normalize text with stemming and lemmatization
steps.instruction: Using the NLTK library, apply stemming to reduce words to their root forms and lemmatization to map words to their dictionary base forms, thereby reducing dimensionality while preserving meaning.

steps.title: Extract numerical features
steps.instruction: Transform the normalized tokens into vector representations:

substeps.instruction: Compute TF‑IDF vectors for each tweet using scikit‑learn (or equivalent).
Optionally generate Word2Vec embeddings for comparison.

steps.title: Construct graph representation
steps.instruction: Create a graph where each tweet is a node; define edges based on document‑level relationships (e.g., shared hashtags, similarity of TF‑IDF vectors) to capture structural dependencies required by a Graph Convolutional Network.

steps.title: Train Graph Convolutional Network
steps.instruction: Feed the graph and node feature matrix (TF‑IDF, optionally BERT embeddings) into a GCN model; train for 100 epochs, monitoring loss, training accuracy, and testing accuracy each epoch.

steps.title: Evaluate model performance
